body.x: Ninewatt Co., Ltd., led by CEO Youngrok Kim, will take part in CES 2027, which runs Jan. 6 to Jan. 9 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Incheon Technopark pavilion, to introduce its AI Solar Development Intelligence Platform.

The company will be at the Venetian Expo's Eureka Park, where its booth number has yet to be confirmed. The platform is aimed at solar developers, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) companies, investors and energy consultants, and it covers the stretch from candidate-site discovery to preliminary feasibility review. Users search by address or parcel number on a map and check land-use and regulatory restrictions. They can also see the grid capacity of substations, transformers and distribution lines, then compare projected generation with internal rate of return (IRR), net present value (NPV) and payback period. Weather and irradiation data and financial assumptions feed into the same analysis.

What sets the platform apart, according to the company, is that site conditions, grid constraints, regulations and finances are reviewed in one workflow instead of across several agencies. That lets users spot issues that need further investigation and rank candidate sites before field surveys and detailed engineering begin.

Founded in 2019, Ninewatt is an energy technology company that uses geospatial and energy data analytics to support energy efficiency and renewable energy decisions for buildings and cities. It develops solutions for building energy analysis, solar feasibility assessment and energy storage systems (ESS). Its project record includes urban ecological mapping and RE100 platform services for the Gyeonggi Research Institute, regional building and road carbon-emission visualization for the Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology, and energy-data analytics services with LS ELECTRIC. It also has solar site analysis experience through the Gyeonggi Climate Platform. Ninewatt received a ministerial award in a geospatial startup competition in 2021, obtained ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 certifications in 2024 and secured investment from LS ELECTRIC. Its separate building energy AI advisor, Opti, was named a CES 2026 Innovation Awards Honoree.

Abroad, Ninewatt is working with Johnson Controls on energy analytics for airports in Hawaii. It has also carried out decarbonization demonstration work with a partner in Japan, taken part in Korea-UK joint R&D and explored business opportunities in France. The company said these activities belong to its existing energy business and are separate from overseas commercial deployments of the solar platform. The United States is the priority market for the platform. At CES 2027, Ninewatt wants to gauge local project-screening needs and test how the platform can be adapted to regional data and regulations, and it is looking for solar developers and EPC companies with candidate sites, geospatial and grid-data providers, and local permitting and engineering specialists.

Next, Ninewatt plans candidate-site pilots with local partners. Initial projects would cover a defined region and analytical scope, checking data availability, how regulatory information is handled, grid screening, and generation and financial analysis. The company intends to widen the service in stages based on the results and to explore supply and partnership models that fit the platform into partners' project-development workflows. Its main challenges are access to land, permitting and grid data that differs by country and region, along with licensing conditions, update frequency and analytical methods suited to local requirements. Results will also need review by local experts and validation in actual development projects. Ninewatt is seeking introductions to data providers, solar developers and EPC companies, advice on local requirements, and support for joint pilots.

AVING News, a global media company with 21 years of experience covering CES, operates AVING CES Newsroom (avingces.news), a dedicated platform for delivering the latest innovations to global audiences. Publishing more than 1,000 articles and conducting hundreds of on-site video interviews annually, AVING News has helped Korean startups gain international visibility and expand their global reach. At CES 2027, AVING News will operate the AVING TECH TALK broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271), providing on-site coverage and interviews that spotlight Korean companies and their latest innovations.

Ahead of CES 2027, AVING News will host the 3rd Innovation Awards Winners Networking Party at MIK BASE CAMP on Wednesday, November 25, at 5 p.m. The event will also feature individual video interviews with participating companies, with registration available through Eventus. In early December, AVING News will begin its pre-show coverage, including an interview program connecting Korean innovators with U.S. media outlets that regularly cover CES and participate in the Innovation Awards judging process.

After CES 2027 concludes, AVING News will co-host a post-show conference with participating companies to highlight their achievements, strengthen their domestic visibility and enhance their corporate reputation.
